safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Omitting a history of aerosinusitis is unlikely to affect acute management of this presentation (suspected allergic/anaphylactic reaction after a wasp sting) and does not materially change immediate triage or treatment decisions. At most, it removes minor background context about atopic/airway history.

safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Neither gold nor transcript clearly states absence of lip swelling; transcript only describes lip tingling/feeling something in lips, not an explicit denial of swelling.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Documenting “no lip swelling” when the patient actually reported abnormal lip sensations could falsely downplay a key anaphylaxis feature (or evolving angioedema) and may reduce perceived severity/urgency if relied upon by downstream clinicians. In a case with breathing difficulty after a sting, mischaracterizing lip involvement can contribute to delayed escalation (e.g., epinephrine readiness) or delayed emergency response.
